key: With my soul have I desired Thee in the night; Yea, with my spirit within me have I sought Thee earnestly; For when Thy judgments are in the earth, The inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
s: In Judah’s song of the strong city, the words turn from the people’s waiting in the way of God’s judgements to a single voice; Rashi, on 26:9, reads ‘in the night’ as the exile, which is like night, and Metzudat David, on 26:9, as the hour when the mind is free of troubling thoughts.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Isaiah 26:9, at [359,9]); one unit, no dash. Plain sense faithful: 26:1 opens the song sung in the land of Judah (“We have a strong city”), 26:8 is the people’s “we have waited for Thee” in the way of God’s judgements, and 26:9 turns to “my soul”, a single voice (Radak on 26:9 remarks on the same shift from plural to singular); no four-word repeat of the key. Rashi on 26:9 (lemma נפשי אויתיך) glosses the night as my exile, which resembles night; Metzudat David on the same lemma takes the night as the time when the mind is free of troubling thoughts. The two genuinely differ and the sentence names both without resolving. Whole chapter 26 of Rashi read for context (the song is of Jerusalem and the redemption from exile, consistent).
